title: Why vampire bats share blood

pendingSeeds.topic: How do bat colonies share food?
How bats navigate in total darkness with echolocation

transcript.content: i read that vampire bats will throw up blood to feed another bat that didnt get to eat. why would they do that, doesnt that hurt themselves
That's a real thing they do. Before we get to why — what happens to a vampire bat if it goes a couple of nights without a blood meal?
i think they die pretty fast? like they cant store much. so if you didnt find blood one night youre in trouble
Right — they starve within about 2-3 nights. So if a bat shares tonight, what might it be counting on later?
that the other bat pays it back when ITS the one that didnt eat. so its like a trade over time not a one time gift. you feed me now i feed you later
You've landed on something biologists call reciprocal altruism. What would have to be true about these bats for that trade to actually work and not get cheated?

they'd have to remember who fed them and who didnt. and live together long enough to pay each other back. and maybe stop sharing with a bat that never gives back, otherwise the takers win and it falls apart

Exactly — memory of individuals, repeated interactions, and a way to withhold from cheaters. You just reconstructed the core conditions for cooperation to be stable. That's a beautiful piece of reasoning.
wait so is this the same reason people help each other? like we remember who helped us
That's a genuinely big question — you're reaching across from bats to human societies. Hold onto that thread.
